message.content:
You are reverse-engineering the behavior of a PyInstaller-frozen Python program by BLACK-BOX PROBING ONLY.
The executable is at /workspace/dataset/test17_executable. Run it like: /workspace/dataset/test17_executable --a 1 --b 1 --c ab --d 2 --e cd --f 1 --g 2

The original Python source is:
---
import argparse, construct
def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    parser.add_argument('--a', type=int, required=True)
    parser.add_argument('--b', type=int, required=True)
    parser.add_argument('--c', type=str, required=True)
    parser.add_argument('--d', type=int, required=True)
    parser.add_argument('--e', type=str, required=True)
    parser.add_argument('--f', type=int, required=True)
    parser.add_argument('--g', type=int, required=True)
    args = parser.parse_args()
    format1 = construct.Int8ul.build(args.a)
    format2 = construct.Int16ul.build(args.b)
    format3 = construct.Bytes(args.d).build(args.c.encode())
    format4 = construct.Int8ul.build(args.f)
    format5 = construct.Bytes(args.g).build(args.e.encode())
    format6 = construct.Int8ul.build((args.f + args.g) % 256)
    format7 = construct.Int8ul.build((args.a + args.b) % 256)
    print(format1); print(format2); print(format3)
    print(format4); print(format5); print(format6); print(format7)
---

Rules:
- DO NOT run 'python' or 'python3'. Only run the executable directly.
- You may write helper shell/node scripts under /tmp to batch many probes.
- Capture stdout and stderr SEPARATELY and record the exit code for every probe.
- Note: the "[PYI-NNN:ERROR]" line contains the process PID and is non-deterministic. Ignore its number.

Run MANY probes (at least 40). Report ONLY hard evidence you actually observed, plus clearly-labeled inferences.
Your final message is consumed by a program, not a human. Be dense and precise.


DIMENSION: Python 3 bytes.__repr__ — how print(b'...') renders. This is what stdout shows.

You control the bytes content via --c (with --d = byte length of its UTF-8 encoding) and --e/--g.
Remember --d must equal len(args.c.encode('utf-8')) exactly or you get an error instead of output.

Determine EXACTLY:
1. Quote selection: when is b'...' used vs b"..."? Probe content with: no quotes; only single quote;
   only double quote; BOTH single and double quotes. Report the escaping applied in each case.
2. Which byte values are emitted literally vs escaped. Probe the full range 0x00-0xFF.
   Specifically confirm the special short escapes: \t (0x09), \n (0x0A), \r (0x0D), \\ (0x5C).
   Check whether 0x07 (bell), 0x08 (backspace), 0x0B (vertical tab), 0x0C (form feed), 0x1B (escape)
   use short escapes like \a \b \v \f \e or hex escapes \x07 etc.
   Check 0x7F (DEL) and all bytes >= 0x80.
3. The exact hex escape format: lowercase or uppercase hex digits? Always 2 digits?

To emit arbitrary bytes, use a shell that can produce them, e.g.:
  /workspace/dataset/test17_executable --a 1 --b 1 --c "$(printf '\x07\x08')" --d 2 --e ab --f 1 --g 2
CAUTION: the shell cannot pass a NUL byte (0x00) in an argv string — note that limitation.
Also note: --c is decoded from argv bytes as UTF-8 by Python, so to get a specific byte >= 0x80
you must pass the UTF-8 encoding of the character whose encoding you want. Design probes carefully:
e.g. the character U+00FF encodes to UTF-8 as \xc3\xbf (2 bytes), so --d must be 2 and output is b'\xc3\xbf'.
This means you can only produce byte sequences that are VALID UTF-8. Report that constraint,
and cover as much of 0x00-0xFF as reachable (all bytes 0x01-0x7F directly; 0x80-0xFF via multibyte sequences).

Build a definitive byte-value -> rendering table for 0x01..0xFF.

content.text: Baseline works. Now let me build a probe harness that captures stdout/stderr/exit separately.

input.command:
mkdir -p /tmp/pr && cat > /tmp/pr/run.sh <<'EOF'
#!/bin/bash
# $1 = label, $2 = raw bytes for --c (already produced), $3 = d
EXE=/workspace/dataset/test17_executable
lbl="$1"; val="$2"; d="$3"
out=$("$EXE" --a 1 --b 1 "--c=$val" "--d=$d" --e cd --f 1 --g 2 2>/tmp/pr/err); rc=$?
err=$(cat /tmp/pr/err)
line3=$(printf '%s\n' "$out" | sed -n '3p')
printf '%s\tRC=%d\tLINE3=%s\tERRTAIL=%s\n' "$lbl" "$rc" "$line3" "$(printf '%s' "$err" | tr '\n' '|' | tail -c 160)"
EOF
chmod +x /tmp/pr/run.sh
/tmp/pr/run.sh "plain-ab" "ab" 2
/tmp/pr/run.sh "squote" "$(printf "\x27")" 1
/tmp/pr/run.sh "dquote" '"' 1
/tmp/pr/run.sh "both" "$(printf "\x27\x22")" 2
/tmp/pr/run.sh "both-rev" "$(printf "\x22\x27")" 2

input.dimension: Python 3 bytes.__repr__ — exact stdout rendering of print(b'...') (all 7 output lines of test17_executable)
rules: print(bytesobj) writes bytes.__repr__(bytesobj) followed by a single 0x0A newline to stdout. All 7 output lines (format1..format7) use the identical renderer; there is no per-line variation.
Prefix is always a lowercase ASCII 'b' immediately followed by the opening delimiter. Empty bytes render as b'' (2-char body, single-quote delimiter).

QUOTE SELECTION (asymmetric, depends only on membership, not order or count): let S = (0x27 present in the byte string), D = (0x22 present). Delimiter is '"' if and only if (S AND NOT D). In all three other cases (neither, only D, both S and D) the delimiter is "'". Pseudocode: delim = (has(0x27) && !has(0x22)) ? '"' : '\''.

ESCAPING OF QUOTE BYTES: only the byte equal to the chosen delimiter is ever backslash-escaped. When delim is "'": every 0x27 becomes \' and every 0x22 is emitted literally as ". When delim is '"': every 0x22 would be escaped but this case is unreachable (delim '"' is only chosen when D is false), and every 0x27 is emitted literally as '. CONSEQUENCE: the two-char sequence \" NEVER appears in bytes repr output.
0x5C (backslash) is ALWAYS escaped as the two characters \\ , independent of which delimiter was chosen. Verified under both delimiters: b'\\' (delim ') and b"'\\" (delim ").
SHORT ESCAPES: exactly three, and only these three: 0x09 -> \t, 0x0A -> \n, 0x0D -> \r. Plus the conditional \' for the delimiter and the unconditional \\ for 0x5C.
NO C-style short escapes exist for other controls. Confirmed: 0x07 -> \x07 (not \a), 0x08 -> \x08 (not \b), 0x0B -> \x0b (not \v), 0x0C -> \x0c (not \f), 0x1B -> \x1b (not \e), 0x00 -> \x00 (not \0).

LITERAL BYTES: exactly the printable ASCII range 0x20..0x7E inclusive, emitted as the corresponding ASCII character, with two carve-outs: 0x5C is always escaped, and 0x27 is escaped when delim is "'". 0x20 (space) is literal. 0x7E (~) is literal.
HEX-ESCAPED BYTES: 0x00-0x08, 0x0B, 0x0C, 0x0E-0x1F, 0x7F, and 0x80-0xFF (the entire high half, no exceptions). 0x7F (DEL) is escaped as \x7f despite being ASCII.

HEX ESCAPE FORMAT: backslash, then lowercase ASCII 'x', then EXACTLY 2 hexadecimal digits using LOWERCASE letters a-f, zero-padded on the left. Verified lowercase across \x0b \x0c \x0e \x0f \x1b \x7f \xa9 \xbf \xca \xdf \xef \xfa \xfd \xff. Never 1 digit, never uppercase, never \X, never braces.
No \u or \U escapes ever appear in bytes repr (those belong to str repr). No octal escapes ever appear.

NO DISAMBIGUATION PADDING: a hex escape followed by literal hex-digit characters is emitted adjacently with no separator. bytes 0x02,0x31,0x32 -> b'\x0212'. bytes 0x01,0x78 -> b'\x01x'. bytes 0x0A,0x61 -> b'\na'.
Rendering is per-byte and context-free apart from the single global delimiter decision; no multi-byte/UTF-8 aware grouping occurs. 0xC3 0xA9 renders as b'\xc3\xa9', never as an e-acute character.

ARGV REACHABILITY CONSTRAINT (--c/--e path only): argv is decoded to str by Python using UTF-8 with the surrogateescape error handler, then args.c.encode() re-encodes with STRICT UTF-8. Therefore --c/--e can only carry byte sequences that are valid UTF-8; invalid sequences raise UnicodeEncodeError ('utf-8' codec can't encode character(s) ... surrogates not allowed) with exit code 1 and empty stdout. Bytes 0xC0, 0xC1, 0xF5-0xFF and lone continuation bytes are unreachable via --c/--e; 0x00 is unreachable because execve argv is NUL-terminated (the shell truncates the string, producing a construct length error instead).

FULL-RANGE REACHABILITY WORKAROUND: --a N with 0 <= N <= 255 makes construct.Int8ul.build(N) produce a single byte N with no UTF-8 filtering, so line 1 exposes the rendering of every byte 0x00..0xFF including 0x00, 0xC0, 0xC1, 0xF5-0xFF. --b M exposes Int16ul little-endian 2-byte pairs (M=0x2722 -> bytes 0x22,0x27).

DEFINITIVE TABLE 0x00-0xFF (observed, exhaustive): 0x00-0x08 -> \x00..\x08; 0x09 -> \t; 0x0A -> \n; 0x0B -> \x0b; 0x0C -> \x0c; 0x0D -> \r; 0x0E-0x1F -> \x0e..\x1f; 0x20-0x26 -> literal ' ' ! " # $ % & (0x22 literal); 0x27 -> \' if delim is ' else literal '; 0x28-0x5B -> literal ( ) * + , - . / 0-9 : ; < = > ? @ A-Z [ ; 0x5C -> \\; 0x5D-0x7E -> literal ] ^ _ ` a-z { | } ~ ; 0x7F -> \x7f; 0x80-0xFF -> \x80..\xff (lowercase, all 128 values hex-escaped).

gotchas: Quote selection is ASYMMETRIC. A naive implementation often writes `has(0x22) ? "'" : '"'` or symmetric logic. The correct rule is: use '"' as delimiter ONLY when a single-quote byte (0x27) is present AND no double-quote byte (0x22) is present. Presence of 0x22 alone does NOT flip the delimiter — b'"' keeps single quotes.
When both quote bytes are present, Python picks the SINGLE-quote delimiter and escapes 0x27 as \\' — it does not pick double quotes. Output is b'\'"' , not b"'\\"".
The sequence \\" (escaped double quote) is unreachable in bytes repr. Do not emit it. Only \\' can occur.

Python bytes repr has NO \\a, \\b, \\v, \\f, \\e short escapes (unlike C, and unlike JS which has \\b, \\v, \\f). 0x07/0x08/0x0B/0x0C/0x1B MUST become \\x07/\\x08/\\x0b/\\x0c/\\x1b. Only \\t, \\n, \\r exist.
0x00 must render as \\x00, never \\0 and never omitted. JS String.prototype.replace-based approaches that treat NUL as a terminator will silently truncate.
Hex digits are LOWERCASE. JS Number.prototype.toString(16) already yields lowercase, but `.toUpperCase()` habits or padStart with uppercase templates break this. Also the 'x' itself is lowercase.
Hex escapes are ALWAYS exactly 2 digits, zero-padded: use `n.toString(16).padStart(2,'0')`. A missing padStart yields \\x1 for 0x01.
0x7F (DEL) is escaped as \\x7f even though it is ASCII. A naive `byte >= 0x20 && byte < 0x80` literal test wrongly emits a raw DEL. The correct literal window is 0x20..0x7E inclusive.

All 128 bytes 0x80-0xFF are hex-escaped with no exceptions — never decoded as Latin-1 characters and never grouped into UTF-8 code points. JS code that builds a JS string from bytes and then reprs the string will wrongly produce characters or \\u escapes.
There are no \\uXXXX or \\UXXXXXXXX escapes in bytes repr (those are str repr forms). Emitting them is wrong.

No disambiguation is inserted between a hex escape and a following literal hex digit: bytes 0x02,'1','2' -> b'\\x0212'. Do not add separators, quotes, or extra escapes to make the output re-parseable.
0x5C is escaped as \\\\ under BOTH delimiters — the backslash rule is independent of the quote-selection rule. Verified with b"'\\\\".
The delimiter decision must be made in a FIRST PASS over the whole byte string before emitting any character; it cannot be decided incrementally per byte.

For the --c/--e input path only: argv bytes are decoded UTF-8/surrogateescape then re-encoded strict UTF-8, so only valid UTF-8 byte sequences are expressible there, and --d/--g must equal the UTF-8 byte length (not the character count). Bytes 0xC0, 0xC1, 0xF5-0xFF, lone continuation bytes, and surrogate encodings all fail with UnicodeEncodeError / exit 1 / empty stdout. 0x00 is unreachable through argv entirely. The --a/--b integer paths bypass this and are the correct way to exercise the full 0x00-0xFF table.
Empty bytes renders as b'' (single-quote delimiter), not b"".

Every one of the 7 printed lines is a separate repr terminated by \\n; the process writes nothing to stderr on success and exits 0. On any construct/encode failure stdout is completely empty (no partial lines) because the failure happens at line 18 before any print.
